Metadata is merged into the entry sidecar; serialization is refreshed in place.

componentObservations.mechanism: A source failure, screenshot/PNG-attachment failure, close failure or measured-JSON attachment failure enters the same ledger. Late serialization exposure does not rely on measured attachment succeeding. records.errors is obtained before the measured attachment attempt, so an attachment error cannot be present in the JSON payload of its own failed attempt; it is nevertheless present in final thrown common-ledger exposure. Subsequent recordError arrivals refresh multi-error primary exposure.

remainingComponentObligations.classification: Unmet retained shared semantic contract; not a seventh authorized Correction11 repair or an assertion that a newly discovered defect was introduced in this patch.
remainingComponentObligations.trigger: The same stored window.__nsLifecycleRecorderError is forwarded by an initial cursor/correlated/passive read and then by another read using the same evidence accumulator, including failure-finalization passive collection.
remainingComponentObligations.consumerVisibleMechanism: Browser producers retain one recorder envelope with one document-local obsOrder. Each Playwright evaluate returns a separately deserialized object: parseResult calls parseSerializedValue, which starts a new refs Map and constructs new objects for serialized object values. The local seenErrors Set only handles references within one assertAndRecordObservationErrors invocation. The ledger likewise deduplicates only original/normalized object references and WeakMap envelope references; materializeEnvelope does not retain obsOrder and there is no document/timeOrigin/occurrence-witness lookup. Consequently two returned objects representing the same retained browser occurrence become two independent normalized Errors and two serialized ledger entries. Catching and re-recording the first normalization does deduplicate, but a later evaluation of the retained envelope does not. This violates the expressly retained rule that forwarding an existing browser occurrence is not a new occurrence.
concreteStaticTrace: A stored recorder envelope E carries documentId=D,timeOrigin=T,obsOrder=K.
evaluatePreActionCursor or evaluateCorrelatedStateAndTime returns E as a newly deserialized Node object E1; the common consumer records normalized N1.
The surface failure/finalization path subsequently calls collectLivePageDiagnostics, whose readPassiveEvents returns the same browser E as another Node object E2.
E2 !== E1, so ledger reference checks and envelopeToNorm miss; a new normalization N2 is appended even though D,T,K identify the same browser observation.
Final exposure contains N1 and N2 as separate occurrences. Their serialization does not retain K, so the exposed records cannot identify the forwarding relationship.
remainingComponentObligations.repairNeeded: Under future separately granted repair authority, retain a scoped internal browser-occurrence witness across normalization/ingestion and deduplicate forwarded instances of that same occurrence, while preserving distinct independently observed errors and their actual order. Keep Node Error identity semantics, stable serialization, domain scoping and no-public-API-change obligations. Do not deduplicate by message, packet sequence alone or unrelated caller-ledger numeric orders.
remainingComponentObligations.execution: Static source trace only; no evaluation, import, test or browser run.

verbatimExcludedScopeCandidate.consumerVisibleMechanism: evaluateActionCandidates returns candidates from the public, replaceable window.__nsRecordedPackets (:146-147). storeHealth (:148) checks only the lifecycle store. In-place mutation of an original packet is detected, because that packet object is also the retained native-action detail. Replacing the array, or replacing an element with a forged object, leaves the retained and private stores untouched, so health stays true. extractActionBracket (observation.js:107-131) then builds the action bracket from the forged packet: rootEventsBefore/After, stateAfter and tCapture/tBubble, which witness.js:44-63 adopts as the Start baseline. This is the same public-store replacement model as N07-04, applied to the packet store.
verbatimExcludedScopeCandidate.title: Bind returned action packets to the integrity-checked native-action records
verbatimExcludedScopeCandidate.repairNeeded: Inside evaluateActionCandidates, derive candidates from, or verify each one against, the closure-retained native-action entries. For example, expose a private read of native-action details by sequence, or verify that each candidate is identical to the retained entry's detail and matches its private JSON clone. Report a recorder:store error when they diverge. evaluatePreActionCursor's lastSeq source (:36-37) needs the same binding.
verbatimExcludedScopeCandidate.scopeDecision: Original N07-04/N07-05 explicitly cover lifecycle store integrity. Extending identical checks to separately replaceable action-packet storage is not automatically a required cutover; no new repair scope authorized.
